issues.legal_issue: A claimant in a land-acquisition compensation appeal should not be denied compensation at the judicially determined market value solely because the claimant initially paid insufficient court fee.
material_facts: The claimants sought enhanced compensation for land acquired by the State.
The High Court determined higher compensation rates and considered the claimants entitled to those rates, but denied them the benefit because they had not initially paid the proper court fee.
Other claimants whose land was acquired in the same proceeding received the enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The claimants had to be given an opportunity to pay the deficit court fee and, upon payment, receive compensation at the enhanced rates determined by the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: Where land is acquired under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the holder is entitled to compensation based on the true market value determined by the court. It is unfair and unjust for the State to avoid that obligation on a technical ground such as an initial deficiency in court fee; the court should allow the deficiency to be made good. The Court relied on the Act’s requirement that compensation reflect market value and did not rely on an earlier case for this ruling.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The proceeding was an appeal concerning compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.court_found_higher_market_value: The court determined that the land’s market value, and therefore the compensation due, was higher than the amount previously awarded.
predicates.claimant_initially_underpaid_court_fee: The claimant had not paid the full court fee initially required for the enhanced compensation claim.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns compensation for acquired land, the court finds a higher market value, and the claimant initially underpaid court fee, the claimant must be allowed to cure the deficiency and receive the enhanced compensation.

issues.legal_issue: The increased statutory solatium and interest apply to compensation proceedings pending at the relevant retroactivity threshold or instituted after it, even when the proceedings ended before the amending legislation commenced.
material_facts: The original compensation awards and an earlier appellate order preceded the relevant retroactivity threshold.
A further appeal was pending at that threshold, and the appellate order in that proceeding was made afterward but before the amending legislation commenced.
A further appeal was pending when the amending legislation commenced.
issues.conclusion: The claimants were entitled to solatium and interest under the amended provisions. The Court applied the increased solatium and the amended interest rates, including the applicable higher rate after the first year.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 15(b) and 18(a) of the Land Acquisition (Amendment) Act, 1984 amended sections 23(2) and 28 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894; section 30(2) made those amended provisions applicable to qualifying awards and appellate orders. The time phrase in section 30(2) governs both awards and appellate orders. Thus, the amendments apply to compensation proceedings pending at the threshold or instituted afterward, even if they terminated before the amending Act commenced. The Court approved State of Punjab v. Mohinder Singh and disagreed with Kamalajammannivaru v. Special Land Acquisition Officer.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: The proceeding concerned the determination of compensation for compulsorily acquired land.
predicates.pending_at_retroactivity_threshold: A compensation proceeding was pending when the legislature’s selected threshold for retrospective application was reached.
predicates.instituted_after_retroactivity_threshold: A compensation proceeding was instituted after the legislature’s selected threshold for retrospective application.

issues.definition: If a compensation proceeding was pending at the retrospective threshold or was instituted afterward, the increased solatium and interest benefits apply.
